style_when: scale is the story — a port, a refinery, a data centre hall, a rail yard, a skyline of cranes — and the reader needs to feel how big it is
prompt: 200mm telephoto compression looking dead down a long big-box store aisle, the sales floor now a warehouse aisle pick path. A multi-tier order-picking cart with grey stack totes stands mid-aisle on the right third, one tote open; plain unbranded boxed goods sit fully stocked on steel shelf gondolas stacked in flat overlapping layers to a bright far doorway. Hard directional light rakes low from the left, laying long clean shadows across polished concrete; crisp crystalline air, deep contrast, prominent steel edge highlights. Palette of safety yellow, graphite and bone white. One-point-perspective asymmetry with generous negative space above the shelving, fine film grain, no people, no text, no logos.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, legible print, watermarks
rationale: This is a systemic operational story about where fulfillment now happens, so the environment must stay legible — a macro detail or studio still would strip the store away. Telephoto compression stacks the shelf gondolas into flat overlapping layers that make the aisle read as fulfillment infrastructure, and the picking cart mid-aisle names the 15-minute pick as the hero. It also breaks the desk's recent treatment run with a depth-and-scale frame.
cue: Your OTIF Never Sees the Pick
subject: an order-picking cart with stacked totes stopped mid-aisle in a big-box store aisle of stocked shelf gondolas
core_thesis: The service level an online order feels is now set inside the store — at a 15-minute pick against a stocked shelf — past the point where a supplier's OTIF scorecard stops looking.
core_conflict: The measured supplier half (on-time in-full to the dock) versus the unmeasured store half (pick speed and shelf availability) that actually owns the delivery promise, staffed and funded entirely on the retailer's side of the wall.
composition: one-point telephoto perspective dead down the aisle, picking cart off-centre on the right third, shelf layers stacked flat to a bright far doorway, generous negative space above the gondolas
